MAActionChangePlayerVehicle.description: Swaps the player's controlled unit into another player configuration (a MAPlayerConfiguration template, such as Mad Dog, Blood Asp or a Battle Armor suit), when its parent trigger fires. The configuration is named by ConfigTemplateUID; the template itself lives in GlobalEntities, not in the mission world.

draw.notes: Actions have no position and are not drawn. Edit them as children of their trigger in the trigger tree.

MAActionChangePlayerVehicle.evidence: 2 retail uses, both as the child of a MATriggerPlayerVehicleType (TPVT) through a logic node. Mission_08 (UID 156066): 'Action - Change Player To Mad Dog', ConfigTemplateUID 33088 = 'Mad Dog Player Configuration'. Mission_15 (UID 197889): 'Action - Change Player To Blood Asp', ConfigTemplateUID 123588 = 'Blood Asp Player Configuration'. Both UIDs resolve in Templates/GlobalEntities.wdf (MAPlayerConfiguration), not in the world file. The configs' CorporealTemplateUID values (the unit template they spawn) are 27828 (Mad Dog) and 123517 (Blood Asp). Code offsets 68-85 (serializer 00199805 / 001996AA).
open_questions: Battle Armor, Elemental, NearClip BA, Turret and VMil_RommelMK2 player configurations exist in GlobalEntities (33072 'BattleArmor Player Configuration' with unit template 32956, and others). No retail action uses them, so their swap is untested.

Mission_08's action sits under a TL 'Is Not Mech (no longer used)' with TriggerEnabled 0, and its TPVT 'Is Mech (no longer used)' is also disabled (TriggerEnabled 0). So the Mad Dog swap never runs in retail.
Mission_15's TPVT 'Is Pilot' is enabled and tests the Avatar flag (on-foot pilot). So the Blood Asp swap is live: an on-foot pilot becomes the Blood Asp.
The config's OwnerControllerTemplateUID, CameraTemplateUID and VechicleNameResourceID are not described here; they belong to MAPlayerConfiguration.
UID 123588 also names an unrelated Env_AcidTree_03 object in Mission_14 (UID collision across files; no effect on resolution here).

MAMech.description: A piloted or empty 'Mech (also Battle Armor suits and on-foot person figures) with per-part hit points, animation, jump jets and the jacking and shake-off minigames. Placed as pad vehicles in multiplayer, as enemies and parked Mechs in missions, and as actors in cinemas. To make an empty one the player can board: Start empty on, Attack pilot 0, Override enable 0 and an MAOwnerController part; in the game, tap Q beside it.

draw.notes: Draw the model named by Corporal3DObj / CorporalMTB at CorporalPos and CorporalHeading; fall back to a box about 8 x 12 x 8 m (Battle Armor 3 x 4 x 3 m) if the model is not in the level archive.

MAMech.evidence: BOARDABILITY, from all 1056 retail MAMech world objects (60 worlds) and the GlobalEntities templates. A Mech the player can walk/jump into is a Mech with no pilot: StartAbandoned = 1 (bit 7 of the dword at entity+0x64, owned by MACorporeal; the MAMech reader also sets that bit from the code-only StartFallen) AND a child MAOwnerController (entry/ownership object: ObjectRadius 4-6 m, TimeToSelfDestruct 30 s, 'Allow Enemy Enter' 1 on 946 of 950, MoverTemplateUID = the Mech template). Multiplayer pad Mechs (543 non-BA + 123 BA): every one has StartAbandoned 1, Nation 0, m_bAIEnabled 0, CanMechJack 1 (BA: 104 of 123), VisibleEntity 1, IsCollidable 1, InitiallyCollidable 0 (518 of 543 non-BA, all BA), ForceUseLowDetail 1 (525 of 543), parent MASpawner (518) or MAGroup (25 loose, InitiallyCollidable 1), children MAOwnerController + MAPowerupDrop salvage. Nation-5 MP pad Mechs (133, MASpawner parents, MAWaypointGroup child, no OwnerController) are AI enemies: StartAbandoned 0, m_bAIEnabled 1. Mission Mechs: abandoned with OwnerController 45 (Nation 0 or 6; Nation 6 = allied Battle Armor in Mission_06a/SPDemoMission), enemy Nation 5 with StartAbandoned 0 and no OwnerController 157, 4 Nation 0 or 6 Mechs with OwnerController but StartAbandoned 0, about 64 Nation 0 StartAbandoned 0 Mechs without OwnerController (parked/neutral props, many in Cinema_* and 3DLobby, some IsPersonMech 1, 8 not collidable, 5 Indestructible). Nation 0 alone does not make a Mech enterable; Indestructible is 0 on all MP Mechs and only a handful of mission/cinema props. Loki (32687) vs Stiletto (124691) templates: StartAbandoned 0, Nation 5, CanMechJack 1, IsBattleArmor 0, IsPersonMech 0, PilotLOS, CanAttach, Buck/Jack tuning and MAGroup parent are the same; neither has an OwnerController child (children are only MAPowerupDrop salvage). They differ in stats, models, WeaponLoadout, MechOrdinalType (13 vs 16), jump-jet fields and the Stiletto-era extra fields (HPRecoveryRate, shield, %dA%d group). Deciding difference is assets, not flags: the Loki template and its loki.mtb, loki_low.NODE and model_low are in boggeddown.mgf / globalentities.boggeddown.wdf (also inyourface, newrivercity, overfalls, rushhour, witchcauldron, Mission_02/06b/13a/15); the Stiletto template, its Player Configuration (124694), Stiletto.mtb, Stiletto_low.NODE and model_low are only in deliverance, illwind, killingfield, ontherocks, newrivercity (and Cinema_1_1a, Mission_05; mountainhigh and troubledwaters have the template in their culled sets but no archive present here). Retail MP pads spawn Stilettos only on those maps (Deliverance 3, IllWind 1, KillingField 1, MountainHigh 3, NewRiverCity 4, OnTheRocks 1, TroubledWaters 1), always StartAbandoned 1 with OwnerController and ForceUseLowDetail 1. Battle Armor pink block: MP archives hold only Model_Low/powerarmor.mgmodel and BattleArmor.mtb; the full-detail Model/powerarmor.mgmodel and powerarmor.node exist only in Mission_01b/02/06a/07/08/16/17a/17b and Cinema_5_4. A BA with ForceUseLowDetail 0 (every mission BA except Mission_06a/SPDemo; 45 of 123 MP BA) has no loadable model in an MP archive; use ForceUseLowDetail 1 as in BoggedDown's 4 BA. Mission_02 starts the player in Battle Armor through its culled player-configuration set (Cougar, Uller, 'NearClip BA' 125891 with a 'NearClip BA Container', Pilot); the world holds no BA MAMech and its MALevelStart has Nation 6, OverrideTemplate 0, TemplateID 0, so the suit is chosen by the player-configuration set (inferred, not traced in code).
open_questions: Exact runtime test for 'player may board': the StartAbandoned bit (entity+0x64 bit 7) is only touched by the MACorporeal serializer (reader 000D9C64, writer 000D85C7, whose writer also saves bit 6 as 1 when debug flag [0x50C85C] is clear) and the MAMech reader (000FC4D0, from StartFallen). The runtime consumer was not located; the MAOwnerController link is inferred from the data correlation, not from code.

Why a neutral Stiletto was not enterable in a playtest: the templates are flag-identical to Loki; the best explanation is that Stiletto's template, player configuration and model files are missing from the base level (BoggedDown). MAOwnerController.description: The 'get in me' behaviour that makes a vehicle boardable by a player. It is a child of a 'Mech, tank or flyer (template or placed copy) and creates the trigger zones around it: where the pilot can climb in (Object*), where a jacked body is entered (JackedObject*) and where the spawner area sits (Spawner*). MoverTemplateUID names the vehicle it controls and links to the player configuration whose CorporealTemplateUID matches; a vehicle without one cannot be boarded.

draw.notes: Child of the vehicle; draw only as a faint sphere of ObjectRadius at ObjectOffset (relative to the vehicle) when the vehicle is selected. Not placed on its own.

MAOwnerController.evidence: 908 world objects (parents MAMech 718, MATank 113, MAFlyer 77) and 42 templates ('Stiletto Owner Controller', 'Battle Armor Owner Controller'...). Every MAMech template in GlobalEntities has one (e.g. Cougar 27265 -> controller 35960, Mission_02's enemy Cougar uses it through the template). MoverTemplateUID always equals the parent's template (BattleArmor controller 35962: Mover 32956 = BattleArmor mech; BoggedDown pad BA instance 126115 -> controller 126113). Property names and offsets from the serializer at 00153B60; meanings of the zone properties are inferred from names and value ranges.
open_questions: The three zones (Object, Jacked, Spawner) are named from the property names only; their exact roles were not traced in game code.

MAPlayerConfiguration.description: The recipe for what a player IS at a given moment: which body template (a 'Mech, Battle Armor, pilot avatar, VTOL, tank or turret), which camera and HUD, the enter/exit/jack animations and sounds, and the owner-controller that makes the body re-enterable. Also used by MAActionChangePlayerVehicle (ConfigTemplateUID) to switch the player mid-mission.

MAPlayerConfiguration.evidence: 61 templates in GlobalEntities (one per drivable thing: 'Stiletto Player Configuration', 'BattleArmor Player Configuration', 'Pilot Player Configuration', VTOL, RommelMk2 tanks, player turrets, cinema stand-ins), all children of MAGroup, 0 in the 60 retail worlds. CorporealTemplateUID resolves to MAMech (BA, Elemental, 'Mech, pilots), MATank, MAFlyer, MAPerson, MACorporeal and MAUberBoss templates (checked by script); OwnerControllerTemplateUID to MAOwnerController templates (0 for pilots/cinema). MARoad.description: One prefab road tile: a flat piece of city road (straight, curve, T, crossing, end cap, ramp, or runway section) loaded from a .road file. Pieces are laid end to end inside a MARoadGroup to make a road; each piece also supplies the AI traffic and sidewalk path points.

draw.notes: NOT a spline: a road is a chain of prefab pieces; there are no control points, width or material fields (those live in the .road file). Draw each piece with the model named by the .road file. Fallback when the model is not loaded: a flat rectangle on the ground, local x from -W to +W, local z from 0 down to -L (boundary box of the .road file; W = 13 m for country roads, 40 m for runways; L = length from the table in the evidence), placed at RoadPosition and yawed by RoadRotation (world = pos + (x cos t + z sin t, -x sin t + z cos t)), Y = ground + 0.15. To lay the next piece: put its RoadPosition at the previous piece's exit attachment point (rotated by the previous yaw) and set its yaw so that (sin t, cos t) = minus the rotated exit outward vector. Exit points (local x,z; outward vector): straights (0,-L), vector (0,-1); shortCurve (-3.43,-17.22) vector (-0.383,-0.924); 90turn (-15,-15) vector (-1,0); shortTee exits (-15,-15) vector (-1,0) and (0,-30) vector (0,-1); intersection exits (-15,-15), (0,-30), (15,-15). Start is always (0,0) with outward vector (0,+1).

MARoad.evidence: Dumped MARoad objects from Mission_02 (53) and NewRiverCity (254); 966 MARoad in 18 worlds, every one child of an MARoadGroup (parent_classes MARoadGroup 966). Reader 0xD59F3, writer 0xD591F, vtable name "Road Piece". Object size 0x144: RoadDefinition at +0xA8, RoadPosition +0xB4, rotation record +0xC0, model pointer +0xC4, AI path point vector +0x8C and +0x9C. .road text format parsed from common archives: [model] model=..\Models\Urban_*\*_rw.node (a RoadWarrior text node + .mesh/.geomVert/.geomFace/.mat, textures Texture_Dump\Roads\Road_013/014/015), [attachments] 2-4 (point, vector) pairs, [boundary] two corner points (country +-13 m wide, runway +-40 m), [Roads] AI path nodes of type PATHNODE_ROAD / SIDEWALK / CENTERLINE with ENTRANCE/EXIT flags. Piece lengths (local -Z): longStraight 60, shortStraight 30, straight15 15, straight5 5, straight15xroot2 21.213, straight15xroot2over2 10.606, end 5 (boundary 10), tee 30, intersection 30, runway_straight 350, runway_approach 130, runway_endzone 90. MARoad is not collidable (IsCollidable 0) and has IsRoadOrTarmac 1 (ground-surface flag for traffic/AI), Indestructible 1, ShadowReceiverType 1. The engine reads only these 3 keys; width, material and children are not stored in the world. Palette sweep 2026-10-23 (ed-palette): MARoad has 0 templates (966 world-only pieces, 872 with TemplateID 0), so a GlobalEntities-template palette never lists it. 16 .road files on disc: roads/country/* x13 (90turn, shortStraight, longStraight, shortCurve, shortTee, intersection, end, straight15, straight5, straight15xroot2, straight15xroot2over2, up10deg, down10deg) and roads/runway/* x3 (runway_straight, runway_approach, runway_endzone); plus models/roads/bridges/env_widebridge01/env_widebridge01_sectiontwo.road, which no retail world references. Verified in game: placed MARoad pieces (RoadDefinition, RoadPosition, RoadRotation yaw, under MAGroup > MARoadGroup) render on a Mission_05-based map when [Assets] ships the .road, its _rw.node model and textures.
open_questions: The shipped up10deg/down10deg .road files are byte-identical in geometry to longStraight (end attachment y = 0), so how the slope is rendered (model, or terrain flattening + Y) was not determined.
The mesh vertex format of the roads\country\Models\*\Meshes\*.mesh/.geomVert files was not decoded here; the models library may already load the *_rw.node files.
Whether the engine snaps/auto-chains pieces at load is unknown; positions are stored absolutely, so the editor must write them itself.
The one MACorporeal child of an MARoad in the slice statistics is probably a mis-parse of sibling links; not investigated.

MASpawner.description: Creates copies of its child object over time: it clones the first child (a 'Mech, tank, soldier, power-up...) with all of that child's own children, up to MaxSpawners total and MaxActiveSpawners at once, one every SpawnRate seconds. In multiplayer every vehicle pad is a MACorporeal 'Env_PlayerSwitchPad' > MASpawner > vehicle (with its owner controller and salvage drops). In missions it releases enemy units, optionally from tunnels (IsAnimated) or when a trigger fires (TriggerEnableID).

draw.notes: Child of a position-giving object (pad MACorporeal, MABuilding, dummy). Draw a small pad/ring marker at the parent position; show the child vehicle model faintly on top. Heading is degrees.

MASpawner.evidence: Tick 0013321F and init 001325B5 read from the XBE: entity +0x78 bit0 = Enabled gates everything; spawn happens only if NumSpawned (+0x98) < MaxSpawners (+0x7C) when MaxSpawners != 0, NumActive (+0x9C) < MaxActiveSpawners (+0x90) when that is != 0, and game time > NextSpawnTime (+0x94); each spawn sets NextSpawnTime = now + SpawnRate (+0x80), increments NumSpawned and NumActive, and clones child[NextSpawEntityIndex] through 00133648; init sets NextSpawnTime = now + SpawnDelay (+0x84) and, if both MaxSpawners and MaxActiveSpawners are 0, forces MaxSpawners = 10. Retail MP pads: MaxSpawners 0, MaxActiveSpawners 1, SpawnRate 11 (916 spawners). Mission_02: spawner 132580 > enemy Cougar (Nation 5, AI group, 2 salvage drops), MaxSpawners 1.
open_questions: How NumActive is decremented (destruction, jacking, leaving the pad) was not traced; the data only shows MP pads with MaxActive 1 and CountJackedAsKilled 0.
InitialID/InitialSecondID: inferred to be reserved network entity IDs; confirm before relying on it (the editor renumbers them anyway).

MATerrainInfo.description: Per-world terrain surface data: a 512x512 map of terrain type flags (out of bounds, border, shallow water, deep water, waterway...), an optional culture map saying where grass, bushes and rocks are scattered, and the footstep particle effects per type. One per world, child of the MATerrain.

draw.notes: Data layer, not an object. Show it as a paint overlay on the terrain: one colour per set bit (use the ImpassableBF*Color0 colours or: 1 red out-of-bounds, 2 yellow border, 4 green, 8 light-blue shallow water, 16 blue deep water, 32 pale cyan waterway). The map is 512x512 u16, row 0 = z 0, covering the full terrain (cell size = terrain extent / 512). Values are bit masks: test (value & ImpassableBF<i>Mask) using the names stored in THIS world, because slot 5 is renamed in 14 worlds. Water cells (8/16/32) should only be painted under a MAWater plane (verified in 6 maps). The culture map (256 or 512 square) is separate and is not an editor concern unless culture scattering is edited.

MATerrainInfo.evidence: All 60 worlds carry one MATerrainInfo (parent MATerrain). Keys decoded: the ~60 hex keys the slice could not name are CRC32 (no final complement) of "<TextureName>BF<i><Field>", "<TextureName>Bitmap/Width/Height/nBits/nBitfields/nUsedBits", TextureName0 = "Impassable", TextureName1 = "culture" (checked: ImpassableBitmap 1F1646EA, ImpassableWidth 9A3F2E9D, cultureBitmap 89FB5118...). Reader 0xF75BA / 0xF7797, constructor-defaults at 0xF736A create 11 types in this order (bit = 1<<index): Impassable - All, Impassable - Ground Movers, Impassable - Non-Mech Ground Movers, Shallow Water, Deep Water, Waterway, Lava, Deep Lava, Impassable - Player, Urban, No AI. Retail files store their own list (5, 6 or 7 fields). Retail cell values per world (% of cells): e.g. NewRiverCity 0 12.3, 1 83.1, 2 2.4, 8 2.2; Mission_02 0 12.7, 1 58.4, 2 4.6, 8 0.6, 16 19.9, 32 3.1, 64 0.6. Decodes the earlier NOTES open item: 4 = Impassable - Non-Mech Ground Movers, 16 = Deep Water, 32 = Waterway (or Impassable to Player/No AI in 14 worlds), 64 = Impassable - Player (Mission_01b, 02, 08, 09b, Cinema_1_3), 128+ only as multi-bit fields. Water cells inside MAWater footprints: NewRiverCity 5,861 in / 0 out; Mission_01b 43,104 in (16 and 32) / 0 out (64 cells are the Impassable-Player bit, not water); BoggedDown 13,253 / 0; MountainHigh 15,081 / 0; Mission_07 39,905 / 0; TroubledWaters 18,746 / 0. Water-typed cells with no MAWater: Cinema_1_1a (15.7%), Cinema_1_4 (9.8%), Cinema_3_1a, Cinema_4_4/4_6, Mission_12 (1.1%).
open_questions: Exact gameplay effect of each bit (who is blocked or slowed) is inferred from names; MAEnvironment holds the per-water-type tuning (speed, damage, cooling...).
Meaning of the higher multi-bit fields ("No AI Go Here" in Mission_05/Deliverance, "WaterWay" in ProvingGround) is not decoded; values such as 192, 320, 2112 combine low bits with the field.
The culture map bit layout (which bits belong to which layer, how density is read) was not decoded.
Lava / Deep Lava / Urban / No AI slots exist only as built-in defaults; no retail world stores them, and no lava object exists in any retail world.

MAWater.description: A water surface: a flat tile (an ordinary MACorporeal with a water-material model) placed at the water height. It draws the animated water and plays splashes; where units can wade, swim or drive is decided separately by the terrain type map.

draw.notes: Water has NO size property; the size is the bounding box of the model in Corporal3DObj. The plane is CENTRED on CorporalPos (tested: the type-map water cells fall inside [pos +- size/2] in 6 of 6 maps checked, 0 cells outside). CorporalPos.y is the water surface height. CorporalHeading is degrees (usually 0; Hesperus oil pools and NoMansLand pools use it). Sizes by model: Env_Water1000x1000 / Water_Sw_1000x1000 (+ _CityNight) 1000x1000; Water_SW_500x500 / Water_Sw_NEW_500x500 500x500; Env_Water_250_250 250x250; Water_Hesperus_Oily_500x500 about 510x510 (bbox +-255.1); Water_Hesperus_Oily_250x250 about 257x257 (+-128.4); Env_waterFall_MD_top pool is NOT square (x -64.7..64.7, z -91.6..86.8, y -6.2..-0.1). Prefer the model bounding box (MGMODEL "info" chunk, min/max floats) over the template name. Draw as a translucent quad, deep colour (100,122,101) fading to shallow (137,137,97) for the normal model; Hesperus oil deep (58,73,57) / shallow (66,78,50); Water_SW_500x500 swamp deep (41,55,18) / shallow (156,187,123); waterfall pool deep (18,32,43) / shallow (123,141,173). The tile does not need to touch the terrain: big maps tile several 1000 m planes edge to edge (Mission_07 uses 4 at 1000 m spacing).

MAWater.evidence: 57 MAWater in 23 of the 60 worlds (+9 templates in GlobalEntities, template_names). Nine distinct models: Env_Water1000x1000 (15 in 7 worlds: Cinema_1_3, Deliverance, InYourFace, Mission_05, Mission_11a, NewRiverCity, TroubledWaters), Env_Water1000x1000_CityNight (4: GoCommando, Mission_01b, Mission_02), Env_Water_1000x1000.NODE (2, OverFalls), Water_Sw_1000x1000 (7: Mission_07, BoggedDown, MountainHigh), Water_SW_500x500 (10: Mission_06a, Mission_08, SPDemoMission), Water_Sw_NEW_500x500.NODE (7: Mission_06b, BoggedDown), Env_Water_250_250 (2: NoMansLand), Water_Hesperus_Oily_250x250 (4: Mission_13a, Mission_15), Water_Hesperus_Oily_500x500 (4: Mission_14, KillingField), Env_waterFall_MD_top (2: OverFalls). Model bounding boxes read from the MGMODEL vertex-buffer "info" chunks in the level archives (e.g. Env_Water1000x1000: 441 verts, min (-500,0,-500) max (500,0,500)). Material is material_water (wave_factor, distort_factor, fresnel_min/max, deep_color, shallow_color, wave texture Water_006_NewWater.tif). Water height vs terrain: type-map water cells are where the plane is above the ground (depth 0..4.4 m for value 8; about 6-8 m for 16). Class is a MACorporeal with only 2 own fields (splash templates); the instances copy the template (IsCollidable 1, Bouncy 1, ForcesCameraUp 1).
open_questions: Collision: IsCollidable is 1 but whether the water plane itself stops things is unknown; wading is tuned by MAEnvironment per-type values and the terrain type map.

Water_Sw_NEW_500x500.NODE (Mission_06b, BoggedDown) is a legacy text node referencing a mesh (plane at y -0.25); Env_Water_1000x1000.NODE (OverFalls) is in no archive on the disc, so its 1000x1000 size is taken from the name.

84E88A5F.label: Hit effect state
84E88A5F.tooltip: Bit flags describing hit-effect state (seen: 0, 2, 3). Individual bits not decoded.
84E88A5F.evidence: Helper serializers 00181966 (write) / 001819AB (read) handle a u16 at struct+4; the struct sits at +0x368 of MAProjectile (callers 000EC597, 000ED2EF) and is also used by 00186A44, 0019767B and 001984A5. At 000F0B52-000F0B6D the word is copied from [obj+0x36C] (with dword [obj+0x370]) into an effect-spawn record, so it carries hit-effect state into spawned effects. No bit tests were found, so the meaning of the bits is unknown. Retail: 0 in 309, 3 in 227, 2 in 7 (MAMech 440, MAProjectile 102, MAEffectChain 1). The owner listed (MACorporeal) is only the shared key.
84E88A5F.name: HitEffectStateFlags

56BF07C0.label: Road piece
56BF07C0.tooltip: Which prefab road piece this is (straight, curve, T, crossing, ramp, end cap, runway).

enum.roads\\country\\ShortCurve.road: Curve, 22.5 degree left bend, 17.2 m ahead / 3.4 m aside (126)
enum.roads\\country\\90turn.road: 90 degree left turn, 15 m x 15 m (84)
enum.roads\\country\\up10deg.road: 60 m piece named up10deg (45); file data is identical to longStraight (flat), the height change is in RoadPosition.y
enum.roads\\country\\straight15xroot2.road: Straight 21.2 m (diagonal of a 15 m square) (14)
enum.roads\\country\\down10deg.road: 60 m piece named down10deg, same data as longStraight (6)
enum.roads\\runway\\runway_endzone.road: Runway end zone 80 m wide x 90 m (2)
enum.roads\\runway\\runway_approach.road: Runway approach 80 m wide x 130 m (2)

56BF07C0.evidence: Read at 0xD5A19 into obj+0xA8. 16 distinct values, all "roads\country\*.road" except runway_{approach,endzone,straight}.road; the .road files ship in each level .mgf (17 distinct files in the 61 archives). Each is a text file giving a model (.node), 2-4 attachment points, a boundary box and AI path points. Default is the most common retail value.
56BF07C0.name: RoadDefinition

729479D1.label: Position
729479D1.tooltip: World position of the piece start (its origin). Pieces run from here along the piece's -Z axis.
729479D1.evidence: Read at 0xD5AFF into obj+0xB4. TESTED: for 799 piece-to-piece joins in all 60 worlds, the next piece RoadPosition equals the previous piece exit attachment point (distance < 0.3 m). Y is terrain height + 0.15 m (median, p5/p95 within 0.02 m in NewRiverCity, Mission_02, Mission_03, RushHour, GoCommando), so the terrain under a road is built flat to the road deck; the editor should place Y = ground height + 0.15. Default is the most common retail value.
729479D1.name: RoadPosition

1DC405D5.label: Rotation
1DC405D5.tooltip: Turn of the piece around the up axis, in radians. Only the first number is used; the other two are always 0.
1DC405D5.evidence: Read at 0xD5AA0 through type-14 converter 0x33FB0 into the rotation record at obj+0xC0. All 966 values are 12 bytes (yaw, 0, 0) (verified from the raw bytes). Yaw is a standard right-handed rotation about +Y: world = pos + (x cos t + z sin t, -x sin t + z cos t) for piece-local (x, z). TESTED on 799 joins: next piece yaw satisfies (sin t_next, cos t_next) = -(rotated exit outward vector of the previous piece), 799/799. 40 distinct yaws, mostly 0, +-pi/2, pi (multiples of pi/8 occur for curves).
1DC405D5.name: RoadRotation

F7D03DA5.label: Rotation (old)
F7D03DA5.tooltip: Old single-angle form of the rotation (radians). Used instead of RoadRotation when it is non-zero.
F7D03DA5.evidence: Reader 0xD5A59: reads it as a float; if it differs from the constant at 0x494080 the reader stores a rotation record {mode 0x201, yaw, 0, 0} and skips RoadRotation. Never present in retail data (all 966 roads carry RoadRotation).
F7D03DA5.name: RoadOrientation

4943107C.evidence: Serializer 0014FB82/0014FC21: int at this+0x90 (entity+0xb0); CounterValue at +0x94 (entity+0xb4). Consumer at 0014FD36-0014FD7B: ecx=[edi+0xb0]; 0 -> sete, 1 -> setg, 2 -> setl, else setne against [edi+0xb4]; the result goes to byte [edi+0xad] and, when true, calls 001452D4 (fire). The count is the sum of [child+0x98] over the trigger's linked entities (0014FCC3-0014FD28). The loader treats it as bool (conv 0x33af0) but the code uses four branches. Retail: 0 in 30, 1 in 7 (2 and 3 never used).

enum.2: Closed loop: wraps from the last point back to the first (code-confirmed)

92B5A944.evidence: Serializer 0012EB0D/0012ED97: int at this+0x58 (entity+0x78); constructor 0012E9ED sets entity+0x78 = 1 (0012EA0D). Consumers read it from the group pointer at [follower+0x170]: 00183E95 'cmp [grp+0x78],2; sete' passes the result as the closed flag to path builder 0019BD2C, which allocates one extra control point and repeats the first point at the end; 00185EAE and 001860C1 'cmp [grp+0x78],2' wrap the position index to 0 once it reaches the point count ([follower+0x1F0]). No branch distinguishes 1, 3 and 4 in the code read (00183D68, 00185D6E, 0018605F), so they are listed as unresolved. Retail: 1 in 880, 2 in 84, 4 in 78, 3 in 1. %dA%d.label: Unnamed numbered group
%dA%d.tooltip: Numbered group of four values on newer Mechs (Stiletto era); purpose unknown.
%dA%d.evidence: Family of 4 members, owner MoeEntity, presence 39%, samples ['0', '1', '1.0'].

Buck%dSimulButtonsChance%d.label: Bucking: simultaneous-button chance
Buck%dSimulButtonsChance%d.tooltip: Chance the shake-off minigame asks for several buttons at once; indexes are stage and button count.
Buck%dSimulButtonsChance%d.evidence: Family of 9 members, owner MAEntity, presence 100%, samples ['0.0'].

Jack%dSimulButtonsChance%d.label: Jacking: simultaneous-button chance
Jack%dSimulButtonsChance%d.tooltip: Chance the jacking minigame asks for several buttons at once; indexes are stage and button count.
Jack%dSimulButtonsChance%d.evidence: Family of 9 members, owner MAEntity, presence 100%, samples ['0.0', '0.1', '0.25', '0.5'].

SetMember%d.label: Set member
SetMember%d.tooltip: UID of an entity set (e.g. Red Stuff / Blue Stuff) this Mech belongs to; the index counts up from 0. Set membership is how teams own things in multiplayer.

PowerupWeaponFireClass%d.label: Gives weapon class %d
PowerupWeaponFireClass%d.tooltip: 1 = picking this up upgrades the weapon class with this index: 0 energy, 1 ballistic, 2 missile (3-5 unused).
PowerupWeaponFireClass%d.evidence: Six values (0..5) per instance; exactly one is 1 on weapon pickups (class 0 on Energy Weapon, 1 on Ballistic, 2 on Missile templates), all 0 on armour pickups.

m_pos%d.label: Marker position
m_pos%d.tooltip: Map position of marker N, in metres (x, height, z).
m_pos%d.evidence: Vec3 in 22 of 23 instances, up to 12 per list (presence 0.957). Values fall inside retail terrain extents (e.g. 1450, 82, 1300).

mname%d.label: Marker name
mname%d.tooltip: Name shown for marker N (for example 'Gate 1', 'Icarus', 'Drop Ship').
mname%d.evidence: Strings in 22 instances (examples: Atlas, Counters, Drop Ship, Gate 1-4, Icarus, Ledge 1-3, MadCat). Name-based; display not checked in game.

ob%dvar%d.label: Objective mission variable
ob%dvar%d.tooltip: Mission variable slot for objective N. Slot 0 is the variable that completes the objective; -1 means unused. Other slots are not traced.
ob%dvar%d.evidence: Slot 0 verified from editor code (triggers.cpp sets ob%dvar0 = objective index; triggers.h) and NOTES.md (completes via MAActionMissionVariableSet VariableState 1). 12,728 of 13,300 slots are -1. Mission_02 objective 0 uses var 8. Slots 1-9 not traced.

ob%dobj%d.label: Objective radar target
ob%dobj%d.tooltip: UID of an object the radar points at for objective N. One per target.
ob%dobj%d.evidence: Mission_02: objective 1's MAObjectiveType has parent 27269 = ob1obj0 (MAMech Scout Mech); objective 8's parent = ob8obj0 (134208). Object UIDs in the same world. Retail values also include template UIDs.

NumObjectiveObjects%d.label: Objective target count
NumObjectiveObjects%d.tooltip: How many radar targets objective N has. Set by the editor from its target list.
NumObjectiveObjects%d.evidence: Mission_02: objective 1 has 1 and ob1obj0 is set; objective 0 has 0. Retail counts 0-12.

NumObjectiveVars%d.label: Objective variable slot count
NumObjectiveVars%d.tooltip: How many mission variable slots objective N has. Keep at 10.
NumObjectiveVars%d.evidence: 10 in all 1,320 retail objective slots (mission worlds). Matches the 10 ob%dvar slots.

ObjectiveItemDesc%d.label: Objective HUD text
ObjectiveItemDesc%d.tooltip: Text id of the line shown for objective N on the HUD and pause menu.
ObjectiveItemDesc%d.evidence: Verified in game: custom ObjectiveItemDesc text shows on the HUD and pause menu (NOTES.md, 2026-10-21). Retail ids: 0 (1072 slots), 0x80000|n (243), others. Editor writes 0xF00000+n (src/core/triggers.cpp).

ObjectiveItemText%d.label: Objective second text
ObjectiveItemText%d.tooltip: Second text id for objective N. Usually 0. Meaning not traced.
ObjectiveItemText%d.evidence: Retail: 0 in 1,289 slots, 0x80000|n in 25, other values in 6. Not written by the editor.

ObjectiveEditorName%d.label: Objective editor name
ObjectiveEditorName%d.tooltip: Name for objective N used in the editor. Not shown in the game.
ObjectiveEditorName%d.evidence: Retail names such as 'Destroy enemies' or 'Base War Red Team'; editor sets it to the objective text (scenario code). 28 slots empty.

ObjectiveEnabledBool%d.label: Objective enabled at start
ObjectiveEnabledBool%d.tooltip: Whether objective N is active from the start of the mission (1 = yes).
ObjectiveEnabledBool%d.evidence: 1 in 251 of 1,320 retail objective slots; all of Mission_02's used objectives are 1. Name-based.

ObjectiveType%d.label: Objective type
ObjectiveType%d.tooltip: Kind of objective N. Affects how it is shown; the enum table is not traced.
ObjectiveType%d.evidence: Retail values in MARoot slots: 0 (1,176), 2 (90), 1 (30), 3 (13), 5 (6), 4 (5). Mission_02: type 1 for 'destroy barge' and 'follow Scout', type 2 for 'climb' and 'traverse'. Enum not traced.

ObjectiveImage%d.label: Objective image
ObjectiveImage%d.tooltip: Image file for objective N. Empty in retail.
ObjectiveImage%d.evidence: Empty in all 1,320 retail objective slots.

mf%d.label: Mission flag
mf%d.tooltip: Mission flag slot N (0 or 1). Meaning not traced; leave as the base mission had it.
mf%d.evidence: 0 in 704 slots, 1 in 616 (retail). Mission_02 sets mf23 = 1 with objective 26 'mfname26'. Use not traced.

mfname%d.label: Mission flag name
mfname%d.tooltip: Name for mission flag N, matching an objective's name in retail (for example 'Get to Beach').
mfname%d.evidence: Set in all 1,320 retail slots. Editor writes the objective text into it (scenario code).

dwVoiceCueID%d.label: Voice cue slot
dwVoiceCueID%d.tooltip: Audio cue id for a voice line in slot N. 0 means none.
dwVoiceCueID%d.evidence: 0 in all 1,320 retail slots. Editor does not write it. Audio clips the editor imports use 0x5C000000+n (triggers.h kAudioBase); whether the engine plays these slots is not traced.

BriefingSound%dCueID.label: Briefing sound cue
BriefingSound%dCueID.tooltip: Audio cue id for briefing sound N. 0 means none.
BriefingSound%dCueID.evidence: 0 in all 220 retail slots (5 per world). Use not traced.

GimpAngSpeed%d.label: Limp turn speed per leg
GimpAngSpeed%d.tooltip: Turn speed multiplier while leg N limps (N = 0 to 5).
GimpAngSpeed%d.evidence: Owner MASpider. Index 0-5 (leg N). Values: 0 1.0, 1 1.0, 2 0.9, 3 0.8, 4 0.7, 5 0.7 (raw properties data, Mission_08).

GimpSpeed%d.label: Limp speed per leg
GimpSpeed%d.tooltip: Speed multiplier while leg N limps (N = 0 to 5).
GimpSpeed%d.evidence: Owner MASpider. Index 0-5. Values: 0 1.0, 1 1.0, 2 0.9, 3 0.9, 4 0.7, 5 0.7 (raw properties data, Mission_08).

PPCBallChance%d.label: Ball attack chance
PPCBallChance%d.tooltip: Chance of a ball attack in attack slot N (N = 0 to 6).
PPCBallChance%d.evidence: Owner MASpider. Index 0-6. Values: 0 0.0, 1 0.0, 2 0.2, 3 0.3, 4 0.7, 5 0.5, 6 0.5 (raw properties data, Mission_08).

PPCBeamChance%d.label: Beam attack chance
PPCBeamChance%d.tooltip: Chance of a beam attack in attack slot N (N = 0 to 6). Pairs with the ball chance.
PPCBeamChance%d.evidence: Owner MASpider. Index 0-6. Values: 0 1.0, 1 1.0, 2 0.8, 3 0.7, 4 0.3, 5 0.5, 6 0.5 (raw properties data, Mission_08).

RushRange%d.label: Rush range per slot
RushRange%d.tooltip: Range in metres of rush slot N (N = 0 to 6).
RushRange%d.evidence: Owner MASpider. Index 0-6. Values: 0 200, 1 200, 2 150, 3 150, 4 100, 5 100, 6 80 (raw properties data, Mission_08).

ImpassableBF%dName.label: Terrain type name
ImpassableBF%dName.tooltip: Name of terrain type bit i. Default names (bits 0-6): Impassable - All, Impassable - Ground Movers, Impassable - Non-Mech Ground Movers, Shallow Water, Deep Water, Waterway, Impassable - Player.
ImpassableBF%dName.evidence: Keys resolved by CRC of "ImpassableBF<i>Name"; i = 0..6 in retail. Value of a map cell = OR of the masks.

ImpassableBF%dShift.label: Terrain type bit position
ImpassableBF%dShift.tooltip: Bit position of type i in the map cell.
ImpassableBF%dShift.evidence: i = 0..6; shift = i in all retail worlds.

ImpassableBF%dMask.label: Terrain type mask
ImpassableBF%dMask.tooltip: Cell value mask of type i (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or a multi-bit mask for the 6-bit "No AI Go Here" / 5-bit "WaterWay" field).

ImpassableBF%dNBits.label: Terrain type width
ImpassableBF%dNBits.tooltip: Number of bits of type i (1, or 5-6 for the multi-level fields).

ImpassableBF%dColor0.label: Terrain type colour
ImpassableBF%dColor0.tooltip: Original tool colour of type i (ARGB).

cultureBF%dName.label: Culture layer name
cultureBF%dName.tooltip: Culture type of layer i (matches an MACultureType Name).

cultureBF%dShift.label: Culture layer bit position

cultureBF%dMask.label: Culture layer mask
cultureBF%dMask.tooltip: Mask of layer i in the culture map cell (only listed for layers 3 and 4 in retail data).
cultureBF%dMask.evidence: Present for BF3 (22 worlds) and BF4 (1).

cultureBF%dNBits.label: Culture layer width
cultureBF%dNBits.tooltip: Number of bits of layer i (1-3).

cultureBF%dColor0.label: Culture layer colour
cultureBF%dColor0.tooltip: Original tool colour of culture layer i (ARGB).

ParticleEffect%d.label: Step effect for terrain type i
ParticleEffect%d.tooltip: Particle file played when a unit steps on type i; empty means none.
ParticleEffect%d.evidence: Read via the 0xF75BA family ("ParticleEffect%d"), i = 0..10 (11 entries = the 11 built-in type slots created at 0xF736A: Impassable-All, Ground Movers, Non-Mech, Shallow Water, Deep Water, Waterway, Lava, Deep Lava, Impassable-Player, Urban, No AI). Retail: 0, 1, 2 and 9 = Env_Mech_FootStep_01.mgparticle, all others empty (60 of 60 worlds identical). Water types therefore have no step effect here; splashes come from MAWater.

WeaponBay%d.label: Weapon bay %d
WeaponBay%d.tooltip: Hardpoint index this slot feeds in bay %d; 4294967295 (-1) means the bay is not used.
WeaponBay%d.evidence: Always 4 values (0..3) per template; 4294967295 or small ints (0, 1). Meaning from name only.

%dCA%d.label: Unnamed numbered setting (CA family)
%dCA%d.tooltip: Numbered unnamed setting; each member holds one fixed number.
%dCA%d.evidence: 4 members (for example 104CA146); sample values 128, 16384, 16777215. Owned by MoeEntity.

%dC%dB%d.label: Unnamed numbered setting (CB family)
%dC%dB%d.tooltip: Numbered unnamed setting; each member holds one fixed number.

%dBF%d.tooltip: Numbered unnamed setting; each member holds one fixed number.
%dBF%d.evidence: 4 members; numeric values 128 and 32. Samples also list HUD sprite paths, so the pattern may over-match. Check.

%dD%dC%d.label: Unnamed numbered setting (DC family)

MinHealthAtReloadForDifficulty%d.label: Minimum health at reload, by difficulty
MinHealthAtReloadForDifficulty%d.tooltip: Fraction of health needed at reload for difficulty level N (0.3 to 0.7 in retail).
MinHealthAtReloadForDifficulty%d.evidence: Name-based. Sample values 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7 listed in member order 0 to 3 (order assumed, not verified).

SS Weapon Icon %d.label: Weapon icon, SS variant %d
SS Weapon Icon %d.tooltip: Second HUD picture for weapon N. What the SS variant is for is not confirmed.

Taunt%dCueID.label: Taunt %d sound
Taunt%dCueID.tooltip: Sound cue played for taunt number N. 0 means no sound.
Taunt%dCueID.evidence: 32 members; Taunt0CueID is 0, the rest are large cue ids (32-bit).

Weapon Icon %d.label: Weapon icon %d
Weapon Icon %d.tooltip: HUD picture shown for weapon number N.
Weapon Icon %d.evidence: 18 members; paths like /Interface/Sprites/HUD/Weapons/acannon_3.tif. Weapon for each number not listed in the slice.

MoeEntitySetMember%d.label: Set member
MoeEntitySetMember%d.tooltip: UID of an object in this set. Member 0 is the first.
MoeEntitySetMember%d.evidence: Numbered family 0 to 31 (32 indexes seen); present on 65% of set records; 479 values, all u32. Sample values 116236, 123095. NOTES.md: team sets (Red Stuff, Blue Stuff) hold buildings; members are UIDs.
